prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1323; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to an intersection in Pasadena, Texas, after a rear-end collision was reported. Driver 2 was stopped at a signal when the vehicle operated by Driver 1 struck the rear of Driver 2's car. The damage to the rear of Driver 2's vehicle is largely consistent with the described impact, and the crush pattern matches the force of the collision. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and was taken for medical evaluation, and the injury described fits the mechanism of this crash. Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle and confirmed this to responding officers, as did two nearby motorists. No prior damage to either vehicle was known to the parties or observed by officers. A traffic camera on a nearby pole was later reviewed, however, and its footage shows no collision at that location during the relevant period. Officers noted this discrepancy and referred the footage for further review. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
